item.title: Zero Trust Branch 8.0.8P5
item.description:
Security and Appliance Hardening Fixes

As a leading zero trust security company that is a member of both Anthropic's Project Glasswing and OpenAI's Trusted Access for Cyber programs, Zscaler has paired its rigorous software development life cycle (SDLC) with frontier AI to surface new categories of risk that traditional security tools miss. These updates are validated, prioritized, and remediated through established SDLC processes by Zscaler ThreatLabz and Security Engineering.

Zscaler remains dedicated to the relentless hardening of our cloud environments and the Zero Trust Exchange (ZTE) against emerging threats. Release 8.0.8P5 incorporates a set of security fixes and internal improvements surfaced by frontier AI models. By design, Zero Trust Branch products are engineered in accordance with zero trust principles to eliminate the attack surface, ensuring they are inherently secure through their architecture. There is no evidence suggesting that any of the risks mitigated by these patches have been exploited.

As part of our managed operations, Zero Trust Branch management services are automatically updated to the latest version, requiring no manual intervention from customers.

For Zero Trust Branch appliances, this 8.0.8P5 release will be accessible as an upgrade option beginning June 2026, allowing customers to schedule the update according to their specific business requirements.

As part of an operational change beginning with this release, the CLI SHELL option is no longer available from the Airgap console for Zero Trust Branch appliances. This ongoing platform hardening does not affect the security or normal operation of the appliance.

New Features and Enhancements

The following enhancements to Zero Trust Branch are supported as part of the 8.0.8P5 release:

  • Option to change the admin password using the Zscaler Admin Console is added.
    See image.
  • Option to change the IPSec remote endpoint (which was previously automatic) is added. To learn more, see Deploying a Zero Trust Branch Appliance.

Resolved Issues

The following issues were resolved:

  • Fixed an issue where failover was not triggered when the primary WAN nexthop was unreachable and the traffic distribution method was configured to None.
  • Fixed an issue where concurrent thread race conditions caused unintended flushing of the FIREWALL-OUTPUT chain and resulted in recurring policy count mismatch alerts.
  • Fixed an issue where security rules were reapplied unnecessarily and resulted in iptables updates occurring without configuration changes.

item.title: Location of Stored ZDX Data
item.description:
ZDX logs and data are now stored in India in addition to the United States, the European Union (Western Europe, Netherlands), Canada, Australia East (New South Wales), or Singapore. Contact your Zscaler Account team for details.

To learn more about Zscaler's retention of logs and data, see ZDX Logs.

item.title: Resource Policy Rule Configuration Enhancements for Microsegmentation
item.description:
There are several enhancements to resource policy rule configuration:

  • Application Port Template: You can select destination ports that are in applications from the Application Catalog.
  • Manual Ports: You have the option to manually select ports for the TCP port ranges instead of using default status ports. Additionally, you can choose to include all available TCP ports.

To learn more, see Configuring Microsegmentation Policies.

item.title: GitHub Repositories App Token Authentication
item.description:
You can authenticate the GitHub Repositories connector using a GitHub App installation token. This method allows for centrally managed, organization-level access that can be scoped to specific repositories and least-privileged permissions. This method is not tied to an individual user account, and uses short-lived tokens to reduce exposure and simplify revocation.

See image.

To learn more, see Configuring the GitHub Repositories Connector.

item.title: Advanced SSPM Support for OpenAI
item.description:
Advanced SSPM supports a new platform, OpenAI. You can onboard an OpenAI tenant from the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal.

See image.

To learn more, see Integrating with OpenAI and Connecting Your Platforms to Advanced SSPM.

item.title: Advanced SSPM Support for Databricks
item.description:
Advanced SSPM supports a new platform, Databricks. You can onboard a Databricks tenant from the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal.

item.title: Browser Extension Version 0.1.36 of Real User Monitoring
item.description:
Zscaler released Browser Extension version 0.1.36 of Real User Monitoring (RUM), which includes:

  • Fixes an issue where the geolocation is incorrect.

item.title: Device Remediation for Standard and Advanced
item.description:
Adds limited access to Device Remediation for Standard and Advanced ZDX subscription levels.

To learn more, see Ranges & Limitations.

item.title: Log Streaming Service (LSS) Support in Microtenants
item.description:
The Log Streaming Service (LSS) is supported at the Microtenant level. Admins can configure and manage log receivers in Microtenants. When the LSS is configured at the Microtenant level, shared application logs are visible for the respective LSS configuration of the Microtenant. If a Microtenant is disabled, then only audit logs are streamed to the log receiver.

See image.

To learn more, see About Microtenants, Sharing Defined Application Segments, and Configuring a Log Receiver.

item.title: Enhancement to Browser EUN Template
item.description:
You can set a caution interval per browser EUN template, which allows you to configure different caution intervals for different browser EUNs. As part of this change, in the Administration > End User Notifications > Browser > EUN Templates > Add Custom Message window, the Caution Interval drop-down menu is added.

See image.

To learn more, see Configuring Browser EUN Template.

item.title: Rerun Job
item.description:
Rerun the job for selected devices and schedule the job at a better time period when the devices are available. You can rerun the job from the Job Details page or from the Device Remediation page.

See image.

To learn more, see Viewing and Managing Device Remediation.

item.title: Support for Snowflake as an API-Based Platform in Advanced SSPM
item.description:
Advanced SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) supports Snowflake as an API-based platform to provide visibility into posture misconfigurations. You can configure Advanced SSPM for Snowflake tenants. Select the SSPM Scan checkbox when onboarding a tenant to enable the Advanced SSPM scan capability for the specific tenant.

See image.

The SSPM Scan checkbox is enabled only when you have Advanced SSPM enabled for your tenant.

To learn more, see What Is Advanced Posture Management? and Adding SaaS Application Tenants.

item.title: Zscaler Cellular Portal Tile Removed from Authentication Service SSO Page
item.description:
The Zscaler Cellular Portal tile is removed from the Authentication Service single sign-on (SSO) page. You can access Zscaler Cellular from Experience Center.

To learn more, see What is Zscaler Cellular?

item.title: Enhancement to Application Service Groups
item.description:
The Application Services page has been enhanced to allow you to define your own application service groups. This page contains the following enhancements:

  • You can add custom application service groups.
  • The Definition column is added.
  • You can view, edit, and filter the application service groups under a new column.

The Custom Application Service Group is available if Advanced Firewall is enabled for your organization.

See image.

To learn more, see Configuring Application Service Groups and About Application Service Groups.

Update to Forwarding Policy, IPS Control Policy, and Firewall Filtering Policy

The Forwarding policy, IPS Control policy, and Firewall Filtering policy allow you to select predefined (AU) and custom (CU) application service groups while configuring these policies.

See image.

To learn more, see Configuring Forwarding Policy, Configuring IPS Control Policy, and Configuring the Firewall Filtering Policy.

Update to Cloud Service API

The cloud service API includes the following new endpoints to create, update, and delete custom application service groups, and retrieve configurations for all custom application service groups (predefined and custom):

  • GET /apps-services
  • POST /apps-services
  • GET /apps-services/{appServiceId}
  • PUT /apps-services/{appServiceId}
  • DELETE /apps-services/{appServiceId}

To learn more, see the API Reference.

item.title: VPN Service Edges Dashboard
item.description:
The VPN Service Edges Dashboard shows the total number of Zscaler Client Connectors, Network Connectors, and VPN Service Edges and their total data transfer to help determine when more resources need to be added.

See image.

To learn more, see Viewing the VPN Service Edges Dashboard.

item.title: Viewing Diagnostics for VPN User Logs
item.description:
On the User Logs Diagnostics page, you can view comprehensive VPN user connection logs and diagnostic data. This page is designed to streamline troubleshooting and provide deeper visibility into organizational connectivity.

See image.

To learn more, see About VPN User Logs Diagnostics.

item.title: Viewing Diagnostics for VPN Traffic Flow Logs
item.description:
On the Traffic Flow Logs Diagnostics page, you can view comprehensive VPN connection traffic flow logs and diagnostic data. This page is designed to streamline troubleshooting and provide deeper visibility into organizational connectivity.

See image.

To learn more, see About VPN Traffic Flow Logs Diagnostics.

item.title: Viewing Diagnostics for VPN Access Policy Data
item.description:
On the Access Policy Data Diagnostics page, you can view comprehensive VPN access policy logs and diagnostic data. This page is designed to streamline troubleshooting and provide deeper visibility into organizational connectivity.

See image.

To learn more, see About VPN Access Policy Data Diagnostics.

item.title: New API Service to Monitor App Connector Health
item.description:
A new Event Monitoring & Notification API service monitors the health of App Connectors to ensure optimal performance and helps you make informed decisions about resource allocations. You can monitor the following health diagnostics, App Connector status, and network detail events:

  • CPU threshold violations
  • Memory threshold violations
  • Disk space alerts
  • Bandwidth utilization events
  • File descriptor exhaustion
  • CPU starvation events
  • Control connection disconnections
  • Connection status (UP/DOWN)
  • Private IP addresses
  • Public IP addresses
  • Authentication events
  • Connector identity and grouping

To learn more, see Understanding the Event Monitoring & Notification API.

item.title: Device Posture Profile Failure Notification
item.description:
You can configure device posture profile failure notifications when you create an access policy. This feature notifies end users when a device posture check fails for associated Zscaler Client Connector posture profiles. Click Manage Notifications in the Add Access Policy window to set up notification messages in the Zscaler Client Connector Portal.

See image.

To learn more, see Configuring Access Policies.

item.title: New Labels and Values in SaaS Security Report
item.description:
Instead of classifying all new applications as Unsanctioned, you can use new Application Status labels Unclassified and Under Review, to classify applications more appropriately. The label Unclassified means the applications haven't been evaluated for risks yet, and Under Review means they are undergoing due diligence.

See image.

Moreover, the SaaS Security Report for each cloud application now displays detailed information about security attributes including their certificate validity, WAF name, CVE ID, breach URL, and so on. More information appears in brackets next to the Yes and No signals.

See image.

To learn more, see About the SaaS Security Report and About the Application Information.

item.title: Enhanced Web Logs: Added Support for DLP Policy Actions and Justification Messages
item.description:
You can filter and view logs for DLP policy actions and DLP confirmation messages. As part of the update, the following changes are available in the Zscaler Admin Console:

Insights Logs

Filters and columns, DLP Policy Action and DLP Confirmation Message, are added to Web Insights Logs and Endpoint DLP Insights Logs.

See image.

To learn more, see Web Insights Logs: Columns, Web Insights Logs: Filters, Endpoint DLP Insights Logs: Columns, and Endpoint DLP Insights Logs: Filters.

NSS Feeds

The fields %s{dlp_policy_action} and %s{dlp_confirm_justification_msg} can be added to the Feed Output Format when configuring an NSS or Cloud NSS feed for web logs. Additionally, the field %s{dlp_confirm_justification_msg} is available for NSS and Cloud NSS feeds for Endpoint DLP logs.

To learn more, see NSS Feed Output Format: Web Logs and NSS Feed Output Format: Endpoint DLP Logs.

item.title: Block Domain Fronting Enhancement
item.description:
In Advanced Settings (Policies > Common Configuration > Advanced > Advanced Settings > Domain Fronting), there are two new options available under Block Domain Fronting:

  • URL Category Exemptions for Block Domain Fronting: Select the URL categories you want to exempt from domain fronting.
  • Exempted Cloud Applications for Block Domain Fronting: Select the cloud app categories or cloud apps you want to exempt from domain fronting.

See image.

To learn more, see Configuring Advanced Settings.

item.title: Time Zone Selection for Time-Related Merge Tags on Notifications
item.description:
You can select the time zone in which the time-related merge tags appear on a user or escalation notification that are created manually or through a workflow. There are several ways to select the time zone. You can select the time zone:

  • On the Incident Details page, when you perform the Notify User or Escalate action for an incident.

    See image.

  • On the custom workflow builder page, when you configure a workflow with a notify tile for a user or escalation notification.

    See image.

  • On the Notification Template page, when you configure an email, Slack, or Microsoft Teams notification template.

    See image.

  • On the Add or Edit Admin Assignment window, when you add or edit an admin assignment.

    See image.

If you do not select the time zone using any of these pages or windows, then the system uses the UTC+00:00 time zone, by default.

To learn more, see Viewing and Managing Incident Details, Managing Workflows, Managing Notification Templates, and Managing Admin Assignments.

item.title: Enhancement to Custom Workflows
item.description:
On the custom workflow builder page, a new Configure Notify Node window is added. This window is conversation based and assists you with configuring a Notify node for a user notification or an escalation notification in a custom workflow. After you click the Notify tile and drag and drop it to the custom workflow design area, this window appears.

See image.

To learn more, see Managing Workflows.

item.title: Additional Support for Microsoft 365 Apps in Advanced SSPM
item.description:
Advanced SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) supports new posture controls as part of the Microsoft 365 connector for the following apps:

  • Microsoft Power Apps
  • Microsoft Power BI
  • Microsoft Purview
  • Microsoft Viva Engage

Existing tenants must grant additional permissions and reauthenticate the connector for these additional posture controls.

Select the SSPM Scan checkbox when onboarding a Microsoft 365 tenant to enable the Advanced SSPM scan capability for the specific tenant.

See image.

The SSPM Scan checkbox is enabled only when you have Advanced SSPM enabled for your tenant.

To learn more, see What Is Advanced Posture Management?, Adding SaaS Application Tenants, and Authorizing a Custom Zscaler Connector for Microsoft Applications.

item.title: OS Selection for Probing Criteria
item.description:
Configure a probe for selected OSs in the Probing Criteria.

See image.

OS selection is supported for end user probe configurations and end user collection configurations.

To learn more, see Configuring a Probe, Managing Collections, and Understanding Probing Criteria Logic.

item.title: Manager Software Updates
item.description:

item.title: Mapping Copilot for Data Sources
item.description:
Mapping Copilot is an AI-guided mapping assistant available in the Security Operations Platform (SecOps Platform). It provides context-aware mapping recommendations to align third-party source data to the SecOps data model based on source-run characteristics (e.g., field names, data types, and value patterns), integration metadata, existing mapping connections, and platform guidelines. Mapping Copilot helps reduce manual mapping, identify the target SecOps entity type, map the key identifier fields, and proposes complex transformation scripts.

You can interact with Mapping Copilot through a chat interface on the mapping page of a data source. Mappings generated through the assistant are marked with an AI icon.

Availability of Mapping Copilot is controlled by the account admin. Mapping Copilot requires at least one successful source run within the last 90 days.

See image.

To learn more, see Using Mapping Copilot and Mapping Data Sources.

item.title: Enterprise Browser for Zero Trust Browser
item.description:
Enterprise Browser for Zero Trust Browser is a dedicated, hardened Chromium browser that protects users from everyday browser-based threats. Users can access private applications for their organization while utilizing browser protection for daily operations such as file transfer, data sharing, and cloud service authentication.

To learn more, see Understanding Enterprise Browser.

item.title: Enterprise Browser for Zero Trust Browser
item.description:
Enterprise Browser for Zero Trust Browser is a dedicated, hardened Chromium browser that protects users from everyday browser-based threats. item.title: Zscaler Admin Console 4.5.5
item.description:
• Fixes a pagination issue that caused incorrect user search results on the Enrolled Devices page.

item.title: Risk Factors for Application Lifecycle
item.description:
The following factors under the Compromise category are available to quantify risk for an application's lifecycle:

  • Application End-of-Life
  • Application End-of-Support

To learn more, see Viewing Risk Factors.

item.title: Updates to Cloud Applications
item.description:
As part of a continuous review, Zscaler has updated cloud applications across various cloud application categories. To obtain the list of cloud applications that have been updated, download the list: Download

Cloud applications are updated in phases. Refer to the trust post for details.

item.title: NSS Support for 3rd-Party App Governance and Posture Management Logs
item.description:
Logs for Zscaler 3rd-Party App Governance and Posture Management are supported by Zscaler's Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS). You can configure NSS and Cloud NSS feeds for both log types to stream their respective data to your security information and event management (SIEM) system, providing a unified view of your organization’s security posture for effective threat management.

Access to these log types requires a subscription to Advanced SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM). To subscribe to Advanced SSPM, contact your Zscaler Account team.

See image.

When creating a policy in 3rd-Party App Governance, you can select the Zscaler Nanolog Streaming Service option to receive alerts for the policy through NSS every time the policy is triggered.

See image.

To learn more, see:

  • Adding NSS Feeds for 3rd-Party App Governance Logs
  • Adding Cloud NSS Feeds for 3rd-Party App Governance Logs
  • NSS Feed Output Format: 3rd-Party App Governance Logs
  • Adding NSS Feeds for Posture Management Logs
  • Adding Cloud NSS Feeds for Posture Management Logs
  • NSS Feed Output Format: Posture Management Logs
  • 3rd-Party App Governance Policies

Enhancement to Cloud Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) API

Two new enum values, POSTURE_CONTROL and APP_GOVERNANCE are added to the nssLogType field in the ZmanageNssFeed model referenced by the /nssFeeds APIs

To learn more, go to the ZmanageNssFeed model from Cloud Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS).

item.title: New Cloud Applications
item.description:
New cloud applications are added to the cloud application categories. You can download the list of newly added cloud applications to the respective categories: Download

The risk index and risk attribute values for these new applications are visible only after they are available on all the clouds. Refer to the trust post for details.

item.title: L4 Ingress Support for Cloud & Branch Connector
item.description:
Cloud & Branch Connector provides Source Network Address Translation (SNAT) and Destination Network Address Translation (DNAT) capabilities in AWS, Azure, and GCP. To learn more, see About Traffic Forwarding and Configuring Traffic Forwarding Rules.

Cloud & Branch Connector supports Azure Gateway Load Balancer via Terraform.

item.title: Amazon Web Services Support in Zscaler Client Connector for VDI
item.description:
Support for Amazon Web Services (AWS), Citrix, and Windows servers in AWS using Zscaler Client Connector for VDI is available for Cloud Connector.

To learn more, see What Is Zscaler Client Connector for VDI? and Customizing Zscaler Client Connector for VDI with Install Options for MSI.

item.title: Unified Dashboard Enhancements
item.description:
Links are added to the Top Sensitive Data At Rest section in the Unified dashboard. This allows you to investigate the relevant files and database tables. For data stored in public cloud and on-premises environments, these links navigate to the Data Inventory.

See image.

To learn more, see Viewing the Data Security Dashboard.

item.title: Support for Selecting DLP Engines to Scan Data
item.description:
Zscaler DLP engines are configured centrally and used for DLP classification engines across channels such as web, email, DSPM, endpoints, and SaaS Security. You can now select specific DLP engines for DSPM and reduce the extra noise from other DLP engines applied to other channels.

All existing DLP engines are assigned to DSPM by default. You can enable or disable the DSPM channel in the Zscaler Admin Console.

See image.

To learn more, see Understanding DLP Engines and Dictionaries and Editing Predefined DLP Engines.

item.title: Saved Views in the Data Inventory and Resource Inventory
item.description:
Saved Views functionality is available for the Data Inventory and Resource Inventory. You can apply filters, show or hide columns in the table, and save this page setting. This allows you to return to the same customized view without having to reapply the settings each time you visit the page.

See image.

To learn more, see About Resource Inventory and Viewing the Data Inventory.

item.title: Identity Inventory Enhancements
item.description:
The Identity Inventory is now more intuitive with clearer, human-readable entity information, new ways to view and filter identities by category, source, and cloud service providers. These improvements are also available in the Access tab on the Resource Inventory page.

The Identity Inventory includes the following new columns:

  • Entity Source: The repository (e.g., AWS Cloud Resource, EntraID) where the identity data is stored.
  • Entity Category: The entity category (e.g., External users, Services).
  • Target Environment: The cloud service providers (e.g., GCP) that the identity can access.

See image.

To learn more, see About Identity Inventory and Viewing the Access Levels.

The following new data posture policies are available:

item.title: Data Duplication Report for SaaS
item.description:
The Data Duplications Report and the Data Duplications tab display files detected in SaaS services for subscriptions that include both DSPM and out-of-the-box (OOB) CASB. You can review identical files across cloud services, on-premises file shares, and SaaS services such as M365, JIRA, Google Drive, and Salesforce.

See image.

To learn more, see About Data Duplications.

item.title: Support for Pattern Matching with AppProtection
item.description:
Pattern matching can be configured for application segments that have AppProtection enabled.

To learn more, see Using Pattern Matching for Application Segments.

item.title: Windows Support for Microsegmentation
item.description:
Microsegmentation supports Microsoft Windows Server 2025.

To learn more, see Supported Versions & OS Compatibility for Microsegmentation.

item.title: Ubuntu Linux Support for Microsegmentation
item.description:
Microsegmentation supports Ubuntu 26.04 LTS.

To learn more, see Supported Versions & OS Compatibility for Microsegmentation.

item.title: Automatic Session Restore for Isolation
item.description: Isolated sessions now automatically restore their web pages if they time out on a user's device. If a session is idle for longer than the timeout of 10 minutes, the isolated page automatically refreshes itself. When this action occurs, the banner notification announcing the start of isolation is disabled. This feature is different from Persistent State, which is enabled per isolation profile to carry over data from an expired session to a new session.

item.title: Agents Exclude Infrastructure Traffic from Flow Logs
item.description:
Agents on the Windows operating system exclude infrastructure traffic (i.e., loopback IP addresses) from the flow logs, reducing noise and improving visibility. With this update, both Windows and Linux agents provide this streamlined flow data for organizations to monitor and analyze.

To learn more, see About Flow Logs.

item.title: Virtual Service Edges Supported for Nutanix
item.description:
Virtual Service Edge configuration is supported on the Nutanix platform. You can download the Nutanix VM image on the Virtual Service Edges page.

To learn more, see Configuring Virtual Service Edges for Internet & SaaS: Nutanix.

item.title: Network Settings Configuration for App Connectors
item.description:
Network settings for App Connectors help improve administrative efficiency and support secure integration. You can configure settings to perform remote commands that enable SSH on the OS, and also update software interface settings across Private Access (ZPA) virtual machines, such as AWS, Azure, and GCP.

See image.

To learn more, see About App Connector Groups.

item.title: Get Network Interfaces Support for App Connectors
item.description:
Private Access (ZPA) supports the Get Network Interfaces command to collect a list of network interfaces used by an App Connector to help with remote troubleshooting.

See image.

To learn more, see Accessing and Viewing Support Information.

item.title: journalctl Support for Remote Troubleshooting
item.description:
Private Access (ZPA) supports the journalctl command for App Connectors, Private Service Edges, Private Cloud Controllers, and Network Connectors to collect service logs or full system logs for remote troubleshooting.

See image.

To learn more, see Accessing and Viewing Support Information or Configuring VPN Diagnostic Sessions.

item.title: Support for Creating Tenants in India Region
item.description:
Authentication Service now provides support for creating tenants in the India region, in addition to the United States and European Union. To enable connectivity with Authentication Service, make sure to allowlist the required IP ranges in your environment.

To learn more, see Authentication Service Logs.

item.title: Real User Monitoring's Browser Extension Version 0.1.37

Zscaler released Browser Extension version 0.1.37 of Real User Monitoring (RUM) to include the following:

  • Adds additional RUM metrics that include remote address, transfer size, and request header content length.
  • Updates the message when collecting RUM metrics.
  • Fixes an issue where unnecessary logs are displayed in the browser console.
  • Enhances and extends log limitations.
  • Enhances security from extension to application.

To update to the latest version, refer to:

  • Chrome Web Store - Zscaler Real User Monitoring (RUM)
  • Microsoft Edge Add-ons - Zscaler Real Time User Monitoring

item.title: Update App Connector Groups for Where Your Apps Are Served
item.description:
You can edit App Connector groups on the Where are my apps being served from? page to resolve unknown app hosting and location details.

See image.

To learn more, see Viewing Where Your Apps Are Served.

item.title: Support for Select All and Hide Deleted for Log Filtering
item.description:
You can select all and hide deleted users, departments, and locations when filtering Insights Logs. As part of the enhancement, the following updates are available in the Zscaler Admin Console:

Insights Logs

The Select All and Hide Deleted options are added to the Users, Departments, and Locations filter in the following Insights Logs pages:

  • Web Insights Logs
  • Firewall Insights Logs
  • DNS Insights Logs
  • Tunnel Insights Logs
  • SaaS Security Insights Logs
  • Endpoint DLP Insights Logs
  • Email DLP Insights Logs

See image.

Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS)

The Select All and Hide Deleted options are added to the Users, Departments, and Locations filters in TCP NSS, MCAS NSS, HTTP NSS, and Cloud NSS feeds for the following log types, as applicable:

  • Web
  • Firewall
  • DNS
  • Tunnel
  • SaaS Security
  • Endpoint DLP
  • Email DLP

See image.

item.title: Step-Up Authentication for Privileged Remote Access
item.description:
Step-up authentication is supported for Privileged Remote Access (PRA) and enhances security by only allowing access to applications after users complete additional authentication. Conditional access is supported for step-up authentication in the Zscaler Admin Console.

To learn more, see Configuring Access Policies and Understanding Step-Up Authentication.

item.title: Business-to-Business (B2B) Federation
item.description:
B2B Federation supports secure sharing of resources between business partners, and allows organizations to establish trusted cross-partner relationships. You can create Partner Federation requests, manage incoming and outgoing requests, and manage federated partners that have established trust. After establishing trust between two organizations, admins can federate application segments to partners and enforce Zero Trust granular controls for shared resources and users. The same functionality is supported via the Private Access (ZPA) cloud service API.

See image.

To learn more, see:

  • Understanding Business-to-Business (B2B) Federation
  • About Federated Partners
  • About Pending Requests for Partners
  • Configuring Business-to-Business Federation
  • Federating Partners Using API

item.title: Zero Trust Branch 8.1.2
item.description:
Zero Trust Branch 8.1.2 includes all features introduced in 8.1.1. If you are upgrading from a version prior to 8.1.1, review the Zero Trust Branch 8.1.1 Release Notes before upgrading to assess potential impacts to your environment, especially the automatic advertisement for IP-based application segments to the LAN-side Layer 3 devices.

New Features and Enhancements

The following enhancements were added as part of the Zero Trust Branch 8.1.2 release:

DTLS-Based Internet & SaaS Connectivity Support and Location Enhancements

Added support for DTLS-based connectivity to Internet & SaaS, enabling secure, higher-throughput tunnels with automatic fallback to TLS when DTLS is unavailable. This update aligns new Zero Trust Branch deployments with Zero Trust Branch groups and sublocations to simplify branch onboarding while providing greater flexibility for transport options.

For existing sites, you can create a new location that supports Zscaler Tunnel (Z-Tunnel) and associate it with the site.

You can enable Zscaler Tunnel (Z-Tunnel) for a site on the Connectivity tab.

See image.

Use DTLS tunnels in Traffic Forwarding policy rules that are currently configured to use IPSec tunnels.

The following location enhancements were added:

  • Support for location templates while adding new sites. This applies only for new deployments. Existing sites and appliances cannot be switched to new location types without full redeployment.

    See image.

  • Location templates provide the default configuration for Internet & SaaS locations. When creating a new site, you can use the default location template. If required, you can create new locations from the Zscaler Admin Console before using those locations with a site.
  • Beginning with version 8.1.2, the new locations created for Zero Trust Branch sites would create corresponding Internet & SaaS locations with VPN credentials with the Workload type. For these sites, you can switch from IPSec tunnel to Zscaler Tunnel (Z-Tunnel).

Custom Internet & SaaS (ZIA) Gateway Objects Support

You can define custom ZIA Gateway objects to steer traffic to specific gateways for policy enforcement, performance, routing, regional compliance requirements, configure primary and secondary gateways with failover for resiliency, and pin sites to a gateway for troubleshooting.

After creating a custom ZIA Gateway, you must use it in the Forwarding policy. You can use up to two ZIA Gateways with a site.

See image.

Support for Hub Deployment in Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services (AWS)

Added support for deploying a hub in AWS and Azure, with downloadable ISO, Virtual Hard Disk (VHD), and Open Virtual Appliance (OVA) images, helping standardize and accelerate cloud-based deployments while reducing manual setup.

For AWS, you must download the OVA image and convert it to Amazon Machine Image (AMI) using the AWS CLI.

You can access these images from Service Portal > Zero Trust Branch > Settings > ZTB Images.

Support for China Deployments

Added support for China deployments in Zero Trust Branch, enabling consistent Zero Trust connectivity for branches in China, including support for bootstrap, provisioning, and back-end communications, custom Internet & SaaS (ZIA) gateway selection, connectivity to China public Internet & SaaS and Private Access data centers, and support for partner-hosted Private Access brokers.

For China-based sites, Zscaler recommends enabling the subcloud and using a custom ZIA Gateway to connect to China data centers. If the subcloud is not used, the Internet & SaaS connection might become unreliable and connections might be routed to data centers outside China.

Support for Internet Group Management Protocol (IGMP) Querier

Added support for the IGMP Querier on Layer 2 VLANs, enabling the Zero Trust Branch appliance to periodically transmit IGMP Query messages and maintain multicast group membership for more reliable multicast traffic across VLANs.

See image.

The IGMP Querier supports IGMPv2 and IGMPv3. Ensure that the appropriate version is configured for your environment.

Private Access (ZPA) Log Level Configuration

Added support for configuring ZPA log levels on Zero Trust Branch appliances.

See image.

ZPA Logs must be enabled only for active appliances.

Management Interface Enhancement

Added support for both in-band and out-of-band management interfaces in Zero Trust Branch to provide stronger management-plane isolation. Admins can configure management access using a loopback interface within the main routing domain or a dedicated physical interface in a separate management Virtual Routing and Forwarding (VRF) instance for isolated access.

See image.

  • If the management interface was reachable in existing versions via LAN or WAN, the management IP address becomes unreachable after the upgrade as it is moved to a separate VRF instance.
  • A gateway must be configured on the management interface to allow access to Zero Trust Branch through the management interface from any network.
  • If the management interface is used to monitor appliances using SNMP over Private Access, only active appliances can be monitored.

Support for Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP)

Added support for LLDP on Zero Trust Branch interfaces to discover neighboring devices and display device information, including device identity, port descriptions, OS versions, and management IP addresses, helping simplify troubleshooting and validate physical connectivity.

See image.

LLDP is enabled by default on LAN, HA, and management interfaces. You can enable it manually on other interfaces as needed. LLDP works only when the out-of-band management interface is configured.

Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) Route Filtering

Added support for BGP prefix filtering using import and export maps to control inbound and outbound route advertisements.

See image.

The route map filters for both import and export options allow filtering by including or excluding IP prefixes.

See image.

The following limitations apply:

  • Network object groups with FQDN members cannot be used for route filtering.
  • Only one export and one import route-map is supported per BGP peer or neighbor.
  • Only user-defined network object groups can be used in route-maps.
  • Route matching supports only IP-based prefix lists. AS-PATH, MED, and Communities are not supported.

System and WAN Health Monitoring

Added support for real-time and historical monitoring of tunnel, connectivity, system and WAN health, including appliance resource utilization, WAN bandwidth usage, interface state changes, and WAN performance metrics. Admins can monitor CPU, memory, disk usage, interface status, throughput, latency, jitter, packet loss, WANMon scores, and timestamped interface Up/Down events, and they can run on-demand WAN speed tests to validate link performance and troubleshoot connectivity issues.

See image.

Weight-Based High Availability (HA)

Added support for weighted interface tracking in Zero Trust Branch HA deployments to enable weight-based failover decisions and reduce unnecessary failovers during transient WAN, interface, or service failures. The weigh-based failover tracks the following components:

CategoryComponents
Services
  • agn-poller
  • securedhcp-relay
  • agn-dhcp-uploader
  • agn-state-monitor
Processes
  • zcc-client
Containers
  • vyos_container
  • policy_container
  • dnsproxy_container
  • zeek

Interface Enhancements

The following enhancements were made to improve interface configuration, status visibility, and connectivity validation:

  • Added interface utilization metrics, throughput calculations, refresh controls, and administrative status management to the Interfaces page.

    See image.

  • Added support to modify speed from the UI. This setting allows manual configuration of the interface speed using a drop-down menu with the following options:

    • GE Interface: Auto (default), 100M, 1G
    • XE Interface: Auto (default), 100M, 1G, 10G
    • Desired Duplex: This feature is provided to support connectivity with legacy equipment requiring specific duplex types. A drop-down menu offers the following options: Auto (default), Half, Full.
    • Desired MTU (Maximum Transmission Unit): A number input field where the maximum permissible value is 9000.
    • Admin Status: This control physically enables (Admin Up) or disables (Admin Down) the interface. Changing the administrative status also reflects in the link status. An Up (default) / Down toggle button is implemented for this purpose.

    See image.

Appliance Admin Console

Added Appliance Admin Console, a command-line interface, for appliance management and troubleshooting, providing configuration (starts with config), operational (starts with run), and status or show (starts with show) commands with improved usability, mandatory password changes on first login, and audit logging to help prevent unintended shell access.

See image.

Site Health Monitoring

The site Overview page includes the following widgets:

  • Connectivity Health: Shows health status of Internet & SaaS IPSec tunnels. It also includes an option to probe Private Access endpoints to check if the endpoints are reachable from the site.
  • Critical Services Health: Shows the status of various components of Zero Trust Branch.

See image.

Low Bandwidth Mode Support

Added low bandwidth mode for Zero Trust Branch appliances running version 8.1.2 or later to optimize performance in bandwidth-constrained environments.

See image.

The following limitations apply when low bandwidth mode is enabled:

  • Asset Discovery is disabled.
  • Configuration updates can take up to an hour if the configuration control channel is unavailable.
  • Requires manual configuration from Zscaler Support for a Private Access setting configuration.

DHCP Enhancements

Address Conflict Detection

Added a check to detect duplicate IP address conflicts before assigning DHCP leases, improving reliability and preventing IP address conflicts in the network.

See image.

Support for DHCP Profiles (Per-VLAN) Option

Zero Trust Branch supports granular control over DHCP configurations with per-VLAN DHCP options, simplifying multi-VLAN deployments by allowing you to configure DHCP options on a per-VLAN basis for enhanced security and operational flexibility. This enhancement allows you to assign different DHCP options to different VLANs, ensuring that corporate devices receive necessary network information while guest devices are isolated from sensitive internal services. Each DHCP profile can be configured for either a DHCP Server (with custom options) or a DHCP Relay.

You can create a DHCP profile and associate it with a VLAN.

See image.

Support for Zscaler Branch Connector Groups

Added support to associate Branch Connector groups with Zero Trust Branch sites for consistent policy application in Internet & SaaS and Private Access.

Support for Internet & SaaS and Private Access Sublocations

Zero Trust Branch syncs with Zscaler Central Authority (CA) for obtaining sublocation definitions and applies labels to traffic origination from those locations within networks managed by Zero Trust Branch. This ensures Private Access differentiates traffic from network segments and applies policies for sublocation traffic originating from a Zero Trust Branch network.

See image.

ENTITY-MIB Support

Added support for ENTITY-MIB for SNMP, which allows capturing host-level metrics, such as CPU and disk usage, through a host-based SNMP proxy service.

UI Enhancements

The following UI enhancements were added:

  • A new field (Comment) to support adding comments while configuring static routes.

    See image.

  • Support for uploading networks and MAC addresses in bulk via CSV files to create objects.

    See image.

  • Option to clone forwarding policies.

    See image.

  • Option to filter security policies based on the Ransomware Kill Switch indicators.

    See image.

  • Support to view (read-only) system default groups.

    See image.

  • An Appliance Inventory page that automatically populates appliance hardware serial numbers and provides visibility into deployed devices and their status, simplifying appliance registration for Zero Touch Provisioning and improving operational oversight.

    See image.

Resolved Issues

The following issues were resolved:

  • Fixed an issue where failover was not triggered when the primary WAN next hop is unreachable and no distribution method was configured.
  • Fixed an issue where certain Zscaler IP addresses were not referenced in default routing policies.

item.title: Zero Trust Branch 8.0.8P5a
item.description:
Resolved Issues

The following issues were resolved:

  • Fixed an issue where log retention enhancements, introduced by certain gateway upgrades in the 8.0.8P5 release, could cause the log upload step to fail silently post-upgrade on certain systems. The fix updates the log upload mechanism, ensuring rotated component logs are reliably uploaded.
  • Fixed an issue where, on high availability (HA) standby gateways, intermittent changes in the standby DROP policy that were preventing border gateway protocol (BGP) peering until a switchover were causing the BGP neighbor state on routed tunnels to flap. The fix streamlines the DROP policy enforcement to prevent policy flaps and peering state bouncing.
  • Fixed an issue where after certain service reboots, LAN-to-Private Access (ZPA) traffic could intermittently fail due to a missing default Private Access route or rule path on the Zero Trust Branch gateway. The fix enhances the periodic self-healing functionality to verify and restore the default Private Access default route, ensuring that the route is always present in the Private Access route table.
  • Fixed an issue where some policy-based routing (PBR) rules were not programmed, which resulted in incorrect routing and forwarding policy behavior. The fix enhances PBR reconciliation, strengthening the resiliency of rules programming.
  • Fixed an issue where PBR rules that match on destination app segments could fail to install on Zero Trust Branch appliances, especially on those where referenced app segments were missing, which resulted in routing issues for matching user traffic. The fix updates how this issue is handled in the PBR retry loop to ensure PBR rules are properly reconciled and installed.
  • Fixed an issue where a gateway upgrade process incorrectly cleared the required web proxy configuration for certain system services, which resulted in syslog and telemetry upload mechanism failures. The fix ensures that the gateway upgrade process correctly restores the web proxy configuration for all system services.
  • Fixed an issue where Zero Trust Branch could incorrectly provide 8.8.8.8 as the DNS server to endpoints instead of the VLAN-configured DNS on DHCPINFORM packets. The fix ensures that Zero Trust Branch now replies with the configured DNS server on DHCPINFORM packets.
  • Fixed an issue where after a reboot, a timing issue sometimes caused the Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) configuration to apply before interfaces were fully operational, which prevented the configuration from being correctly applied and intermittently caused OSPF adjacency failures in Virtual Routing and Forwarding deployments. The fix updates the configuration reconciliation logic to handle these circumstances and ensures the OSPF configuration is properly applied on reboot.

item.title: Zero Trust Branch 8.0.8P5b
item.description:
Resolved Issues

The following issues were resolved:

  • Fixed an issue where the DHCP server failed to parse Vendor Class Identifier (VCI) filters containing spaces, which prevented the server from offering all configured DHCP options and resulted in access points failing to receive IP addresses.
  • Fixed an issue where the DHCP server incorrectly offered IP addresses from a customer's previous VLAN scope when a device transitioned between VLANs, resulting in assignment failures and endpoints defaulting to Automatic Private IP Addressing (APIPA).
  • Fixed an issue where the ebondx WAN IP address failed to restore following a port channel bounce on the peer link.
  • Fixed an issue where the DHCP server incorrectly acknowledged requested IP addresses that were already assigned to other clients, causing duplicate IP issues. The fix ensures the server now sends a DHCP Negative Acknowledgement (NAK) packet when a requested IP is unavailable, forcing the client to restart the DHCP process to obtain a unique address.
  • Fixed an issue where DHCPDECLINE packets did not trigger a release event to the backend, resulting in stale or incorrect entries on the Assets page (Asset Intelligence > Assets)
  • Fixed an issue where default routes were repeatedly added to and deleted from the IPSec route table, leading to intermittent internet connectivity issues.
  • Fixed an issue where IP addresses were prematurely deleted from the lease table after a NAK was sent, which could lead to duplicate IP assignments. The fix ensures these IPs are moved to a "ping-check-failed" state for one hour to prevent them from being reassigned to other devices.
  • Fixed an issue where the connection tracking (conntrack) table was incorrectly sized for the hardware form factor, preventing potential table overflows and client disconnects in large scale deployments.

item.title: TCP Type Enhancements
item.description:
You can select a specific TCP traceroute when you configure a Cloud Path probe:

  • Resilient TCP Type: Traceroute when the TCP connection fails and then retries using the Conventional TCP type.
  • Strict TCP Type: Traceroute when the TCP connection fails and there are no other connections to fall back to.

The Conventional TCP type is the original TCP traceroute based on sync (SYN) packets and is potentially blocked by firewalls.

Any probe configured with a TCP type prior to this enhancement defaults to a Resilient TCP type configuration. If you want to continue using the Conventional TCP type, configure your existing probe to select Conventional TCP Type.

See image.

To learn more, see Configuring a Probe and Supported Versions & Feature Compatibility.

item.title: Support for External Link Expiration in Google Drive
item.description:
You can set a periodic or custom expiration period for your Google Drive links (internal or external). Access to the files is automatically revoked after the expiration period.

In the Edit DLP rule window, four new actions with expiration have been added:

  • Remove Collaborators After Expiry
  • Remove External Sharing Links After Expiry
  • Remove Internal Sharing Links After Expiry
  • Remove Sharing After Expiry

See image.

Additionally, you can also set manual expiration for Google Drive under Remediation Actions on the SaaS Assets with Incidents page.

To learn more, see:

  • Configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy with Content Inspection
  • Configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy without Content Inspection
  • Understanding SaaS Security API Supported Capabilities Draft
  • Understanding the Assets Report: Assets with Incidents

Enhancements to the SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning Data Loss Prevention (DLP) APIs

Enum values OFLCASB_DLP_REMOVE_COLLABORATORS_EXPIRY, OFLCASB_DLP_REMOVE_SHARING_EXPIRY, OFLCASB_DLP_REMOVE_INTERNAL_LINK_SHARE_EXPIRY, and OFLCASB_DLP_REMOVE_EXTERNAL_LINK_SHARE_EXPIRY are added to the action field in the CASBDlpRule model referenced by the /casbDlpRules APIs. For a Google Drive tenant, these enum values allow you to:

  • remove collaborators after expiration
  • remove sharing after expiration
  • remove internal sharing links after expiration
  • remove external sharing links after expiration

Additionally, two new fields, fileSharingExpiryTimeType and fileSharingExpiryTime are available in the CASBDlpRule model referenced by the /casbDlpRules APIs. These fields are required to set the file sharing expiration period. To learn more, go to the CASBDlpRule model from SaaS Security API.

item.title: Secure Email Gateway Support in Outbound Email DLP Policies
item.description:
You can use Zscaler Outbound Email Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies with your secure email gateway (SEG) to prevent the exfiltration of sensitive data by enforcing policy rules on email content sent to external domains, including content in subject lines, body text, and attachments. As part of your larger DLP strategy, Zscaler Outbound Email DLP for SEGs lets you use the same DLP policy tools that you already use across other channels (i.e., Inline Web DLP, Endpoint DLP, and SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning DLP), eliminating the need for different DLP point solutions and the operational overhead involved in maintaining those solutions. Additionally, you can monitor outbound email activity with dashboards, reports, and NSS feeds. This enhancement supplements existing Outbound Email DLP support for Microsoft Exchange and Gmail.

Because of recent enhancements to next-hop validation that enforce stricter security checks during SMTP connections, the Zscaler service:

  • Strictly enforces SSL/TLS for secure SMTP connections.
  • Performs server certificate validation that requires the presented certificate to be valid and trusted.
  • Does not allow self-signed, expired, or otherwise invalid certificates.

As you set up Email tenants in the Zscaler Admin Console (Policies > Data Protection > Policy > Email Tenants), you have the option to select an SEG tenant.

See image.

To learn more, see Adding Email Tenants and Configuring SEGs for Zscaler Outbound Email DLP.

item.description:
You can clone predefined Data Loss Prevention (DLP) sub-dictionaries. Predefined DLP sub-dictionaries are hierarchical child dictionaries associated with predefined DLP dictionaries. Cloning a predefined DLP sub-dictionary creates a separate copy that you can customize with different confidence score thresholds and other dictionary-specific parameters without modifying the original sub-dictionary.

See image.

item.title: Added Support for Enhanced Dictionaries and Sub-Dictionaries
item.description:
The Zscaler service supports the following predefined Data Loss Prevention (DLP) dictionaries:

  • Enhanced Credentials and Secrets
  • Enhanced International Bank Account Number (IBAN)
  • Enhanced Passport Number (Asia)
  • Enhanced Passport Number (European Union)

The parent dictionaries contain predefined sub-dictionaries, and each sub-dictionary can be individually referenced in your DLP engines.

On the DLP Dictionaries & Engines page (Policies > Data Protection > Common Resources > DLP Dictionaries & Engines), you can expand each dictionary's section to see its sub-dictionary. You can configure each of the individual sub-dictionaries to set the Confidence Score Threshold, Proximity Length, and any Custom High Confidence Phrases.

See image.

  • The Enhanced dictionaries for Credentials and Secrets, Driver License (US), International Bank Account Number, Passport Number (Asia), and Passport Number (European Union) are not supported for Endpoint DLP.
  • The legacy dictionaries for Credentials and Secrets, Driver License (US), International Bank Account Number, Passport Number (Asia), and Passport Number (European Union) have been replaced, but not deprecated, by the Enhanced Credentials and Secrets, Enhanced Driver License (US), Enhanced International Bank Account Number, Enhanced Passport Number (Asia), and Enhanced Passport Number (European Union) predefined dictionaries.

To learn more, see Understanding Predefined DLP Dictionaries.
